description: Static, read-only SQL Server / Azure SQL Database probe catalog for future Microsoft.Data.SqlClient collection. Every probe is a static SELECT/CTE/APPLY plus safe session SET statements; no dynamic SQL, no mutating statements. See sql/README.md for permission tables, unit conventions, and cadence/overhead guidance.

connectionScopes.server: Instance-wide facts; the query itself is not tied to a particular user database, though the connection can be opened against any database that grants the required permission.
connectionScopes.master: Conventionally run against the master database; the underlying catalog view is visible from any database context on-box, but Azure SQL Database restricts the visible row set (see the probe's azureSqlDatabase notes).
connectionScopes.database: Assumes the client already opened (or switched pooled connections to) the specific target database. The probe only reports on that database.
connectionScopes.tempdb: Assumes the client explicitly opened its connection with tempdb as the current database. Unlike 'database', this is never the application's own business database.

cadenceClasses.realtime: Sub-minute polling; designed for live dashboards of active work (sessions, waits, blocking).
cadenceClasses.frequent: 1-5 minute polling; cheap, high-value operational counters.
cadenceClasses.standard: 5-15 minute polling; Query Store summaries, space, and index usage roll-ups.
cadenceClasses.low_frequency: 15-60+ minute polling; identity and configuration facts that rarely change.
cadenceClasses.on_demand: Only run in response to a specific, already-identified object; never on a fixed timer.

relativeCosts.trivial: In-memory counters or fixed-size DMVs; no page or plan-cache scan.
relativeCosts.low: Small, bounded in-memory scan (session/request/task lists, single-database catalog joins).
relativeCosts.medium: Bounded by an explicit parameter (time window, TopN, or a required object id); cost scales with that bound, not with database size.
relativeCosts.high: Not used in this catalog; any probe that would require this cost class needs an explicit bound before it may be added.

probes.title: Server/platform identity

azureSqlDatabase.notes: Supported (EngineEdition = 5). cpu_count/physical_memory_kb might reflect the host or elastic-pool machine's resources, not the tenant's assigned vCore/DTU capacity -- see sys.dm_user_db_resource_governance.cpu_limit and sys.dm_os_job_object.process_memory_limit_mb for the tenant's actual compute limits. This probe deliberately omits sys.dm_os_host_info (see server.host_info), which is not supported on Azure SQL Database.

probes.requiredPermission: SERVERPROPERTY(): none. sys.dm_os_sys_info: VIEW SERVER STATE (SQL Server 2019 and earlier) or VIEW SERVER PERFORMANCE STATE (SQL Server 2022+).
probes.resultContract: Exactly one row: server/instance identity, edition, engine edition, CPU/scheduler/memory sizing, and start time.

probes.title: Host operating system platform detail

azureSqlDatabase.notes: sys.dm_os_host_info's documented platform list is SQL Server and Azure SQL Managed Instance only; it does not include Azure SQL Database and the call fails there. Use server.identity alone on Azure SQL Database; only run this probe when server.identity.engine_edition indicates SQL Server (1/2/3/4) or Managed Instance (8).

probes.requiredPermission: VIEW SERVER STATE (SQL Server 2019 and earlier) or VIEW SERVER PERFORMANCE STATE (SQL Server 2022+).
probes.resultContract: Exactly one row: host operating system platform, distribution, release, and service-pack level for the connected SQL Server or Managed Instance.

probes.title: Visible database inventory

azureSqlDatabase.notes: Supported, but row visibility depends on connection context and permission, not a blanket restriction. Connected to the 'master' database with sufficient permission (e.g. server admin/Microsoft Entra admin), sys.databases can enumerate every database visible on the logical server. Connected to a user database, sys.databases returns only 'master' and that database itself -- it cannot enumerate sibling databases on the server. Run this probe against a 'master' connection when full-server enumeration is required; otherwise treat it as reporting only the current database plus 'master'.

probes.requiredPermission: VIEW ANY DATABASE (granted to PUBLIC by default since SQL Server 2016 SP1).
probes.resultContract: Zero or more rows, one per visible database: id, name, state, recovery model, containment, compatibility level, Query Store on/off, collation, create date.

probes.title: Current database identity

azureSqlDatabase.notes: Supported and intentionally limited to DB_ID() on the current connection.

probes.requiredPermission: Ordinary access to the current database.
probes.resultContract: Exactly one row for DB_ID(): connection-local database id, name, state, compatibility level, and Query Store on/off. The id is not a globally stable Azure database identity.

probes.title: Query Store options (base, SQL Server 2016-2017)
probes.versionVariantNotes: Base column set only; use querystore.options_2019 on SQL Server 2019+/Azure SQL Database for the CUSTOM capture-policy columns.

azureSqlDatabase.notes: Supported, but prefer querystore.options_2019 on Azure SQL Database since it always runs a current engine.

probes.requiredPermission: VIEW DATABASE STATE (SQL Server 2016-2019) or VIEW DATABASE PERFORMANCE STATE (SQL Server 2022+).
probes.resultContract: actual_state/actual_state_desc = 0/'OFF' is the reliable signal that Query Store is not currently capturing data; row absence is not a documented signal (Microsoft does not specify row-count behavior for a database that never enabled Query Store). When present, exactly one row describing desired/actual state, size limits, retention, and capture mode.

probes.title: Query Store options (CUSTOM capture policy, SQL Server 2019+)
probes.versionVariantNotes: Adds wait_stats_capture_mode (2017+) and capture_policy_* CUSTOM-mode columns (2019+); querying these on SQL Server 2016/2017 raises 'Invalid column name'. Use querystore.options_2016 there instead.

azureSqlDatabase.notes: Supported.

probes.requiredPermission: VIEW DATABASE STATE (SQL Server 2019) or VIEW DATABASE PERFORMANCE STATE (SQL Server 2022+).
probes.resultContract: actual_state/actual_state_desc = 0/'OFF' is the reliable signal that Query Store is not currently capturing data; row absence is not a documented signal (Microsoft does not specify row-count behavior for a database that never enabled Query Store). When present, exactly one row including CUSTOM capture-policy thresholds and wait-stats capture mode.

probes.title: Query Store query identity and compile statistics

azureSqlDatabase.notes: Supported.

probes.requiredPermission: VIEW DATABASE STATE (SQL Server 2016-2019) or VIEW DATABASE PERFORMANCE STATE (SQL Server 2022+).

parameters.name: @StartTime
parameters.description: Inclusive lower bound on last_execution_time. Callers should pass a bounded, recent window (e.g. now - collection interval).

parameters.name: @TopN
parameters.description: Caps the row count via TOP(@TopN). Must be a small, positive, application-chosen bound.

probes.resultContract: At most @TopN rows ordered by last_execution_time descending: query identity, parameterization type, and compile-time statistics in microseconds/KiB. No plan or runtime execution data.

probes.title: Query Store plan metadata (base, SQL Server 2016 only)
probes.versionVariantNotes: plan_forcing_type/plan_forcing_type_desc do not exist as columns until SQL Server 2017 (14.x); referencing them on SQL Server 2016 raises 'Invalid column name', so this variant omits them entirely rather than expecting NULL. Use querystore.plan_summary_2017 on SQL Server 2017 (14.x) through 2019 (15.x), or querystore.plan_summary_2022 on SQL Server 2022 (16.x)+/Azure SQL Database.

azureSqlDatabase.notes: Supported, but prefer querystore.plan_summary_2022 since Azure SQL Database always runs a current engine and this variant's column set is strictly the oldest and smallest.

probes.requiredPermission: VIEW DATABASE STATE on the database.

parameters.name: @StartTime
parameters.description: Inclusive lower bound on last_execution_time.

parameters.name: @TopN
parameters.description: Caps the row count via TOP(@TopN).

probes.resultContract: At most @TopN rows ordered by last_execution_time descending: base plan identity and compile duration in microseconds. No plan-forcing-type columns (SQL Server 2016 does not have them). query_plan (Showplan XML) is deliberately excluded.

probes.title: Query Store plan metadata with plan-forcing type (SQL Server 2017-2019)
probes.versionVariantNotes: Adds plan_forcing_type/plan_forcing_type_desc (SQL Server 2017 (14.x)+) over the 2016 base. Does not include has_compile_replay_script, is_optimized_plan_forcing_disabled, plan_type, plan_type_desc, which do not exist before SQL Server 2022 (16.x) and raise 'Invalid column name' there -- use querystore.plan_summary_2022 for those. Use querystore.plan_summary_2016 on SQL Server 2016 (13.x) only.

azureSqlDatabase.notes: Supported, but prefer querystore.plan_summary_2022 since Azure SQL Database always runs a current engine.

probes.requiredPermission: VIEW DATABASE STATE (SQL Server 2017-2019) or VIEW DATABASE PERFORMANCE STATE (SQL Server 2022+).

parameters.name: @StartTime
parameters.description: Inclusive lower bound on last_execution_time.

parameters.name: @TopN
parameters.description: Caps the row count via TOP(@TopN).

probes.resultContract: At most @TopN rows ordered by last_execution_time descending: plan identity, forcing state (plan_forcing_type_desc), and compile duration in microseconds. query_plan (Showplan XML) is deliberately excluded.

probes.title: Query Store plan metadata with parameter-sensitive-plan variants (SQL Server 2022+)
probes.versionVariantNotes: has_compile_replay_script, is_optimized_plan_forcing_disabled, plan_type, plan_type_desc do not exist before SQL Server 2022 and raise 'Invalid column name' there. Use querystore.plan_summary_2016 for SQL Server 2016 (13.x) only, or querystore.plan_summary_2017 for SQL Server 2017 (14.x) through 2019 (15.x).

azureSqlDatabase.notes: Supported.

probes.requiredPermission: VIEW DATABASE PERFORMANCE STATE on the database.

parameters.name: @StartTime
parameters.description: Inclusive lower bound on last_execution_time.

parameters.name: @TopN
parameters.description: Caps the row count via TOP(@TopN).

probes.resultContract: At most @TopN rows ordered by last_execution_time descending: base plan metadata plus plan_type_desc distinguishing Compiled/Dispatcher/Query Variant plans. query_plan (Showplan XML) is deliberately excluded.

probes.title: Query Store runtime execution statistics (weighted, de-duplicated, base)
probes.versionVariantNotes: replica_group_id does not exist as a column before SQL Server 2022 (16.x) and raises 'Invalid column name' if selected there, so this variant omits it. Use querystore.runtime_stats_summary_2022 on SQL Server 2022 (16.x)+ so secondary-replica runtime stats are kept separate instead of silently summed together.

azureSqlDatabase.notes: Supported, but prefer querystore.runtime_stats_summary_2022 since Azure SQL Database always runs a current engine.

probes.requiredPermission: VIEW DATABASE STATE on the database.

parameters.name: @StartTime
parameters.description: Inclusive lower bound on the runtime-stats interval start_time.

parameters.name: @EndTime
parameters.description: Exclusive upper bound on the runtime-stats interval start_time.

probes.resultContract: Zero or more rows, one per (plan_id, runtime_stats_interval_id, execution_type), already SUMmed across any duplicate active-interval rows. Durations/CPU are microseconds; IO columns are 8-KiB pages; weighted_avg_duration_us is execution-count-weighted, separated by execution_type_desc (Regular/Aborted/Exception). No replica identifier.

probes.title: Query Store runtime execution statistics with replica separation (SQL Server 2022+)
probes.versionVariantNotes: Adds and groups by replica_group_id (SQL Server 2022 (16.x)+), which does not exist and raises 'Invalid column name' on older engines. Use querystore.runtime_stats_summary_2016 on SQL Server 2016 (13.x) through 2019 (15.x).

azureSqlDatabase.notes: Supported.

probes.requiredPermission: VIEW DATABASE PERFORMANCE STATE on the database.

parameters.name: @StartTime
parameters.description: Inclusive lower bound on the runtime-stats interval start_time.

parameters.name: @EndTime
parameters.description: Exclusive upper bound on the runtime-stats interval start_time.

probes.resultContract: Zero or more rows, one per (plan_id, runtime_stats_interval_id, execution_type, replica_group_id), already SUMmed across any duplicate active-interval rows. Durations/CPU are microseconds; IO columns are 8-KiB pages; weighted_avg_duration_us is execution-count-weighted, separated by execution_type_desc (Regular/Aborted/Exception) and replica_group_id so secondary-replica runtime is never combined with the primary's.

probes.title: Bounded database Query Store workload summary
probes.versionVariantNotes: Base variant without replica_group_id. Atlas consumes this bounded database aggregate rather than plan-by-interval detail.

azureSqlDatabase.notes: Supported; use the 2022 variant when replica_group_id metadata is present.

probes.requiredPermission: VIEW DATABASE STATE on the database.

parameters.name: @StartTime
parameters.description: Inclusive lower bound on runtime-stats interval start_time.

parameters.name: @EndTime
parameters.description: Exclusive upper bound on runtime-stats interval start_time.

probes.resultContract: At most one aggregate row per execution_type after active-interval duplicate consolidation. Execution count remains exact decimal(38,0). Duration/CPU microseconds and logical-read 8-KiB pages preserve source float fractions through weighting and both sums, then round once to checked decimal(38,0) integral totals. Regular, Aborted, and Exception rows remain separate. No query text or plan XML.

probes.title: Bounded replica-aware Query Store workload summary
probes.versionVariantNotes: Uses replica_group_id during active-interval consolidation before producing one database-wide row per execution type. Use the 2016 variant when metadata does not expose that column.

azureSqlDatabase.notes: Supported when capability metadata confirms replica_group_id.

probes.requiredPermission: VIEW DATABASE PERFORMANCE STATE on the database.

parameters.name: @StartTime
parameters.description: Inclusive lower bound on runtime-stats interval start_time.

parameters.name: @EndTime
parameters.description: Exclusive upper bound on runtime-stats interval start_time.

probes.resultContract: At most one database-wide aggregate row per execution_type after replica-aware active-interval duplicate consolidation. Execution count remains exact decimal(38,0). Duration/CPU microseconds and logical-read 8-KiB pages preserve source float fractions through weighting and both sums, then round once to checked decimal(38,0) integral totals. Regular, Aborted, and Exception rows remain separate. No query text or plan XML.

probes.title: Query Store wait statistics (base, SQL Server 2017-2019)
probes.versionVariantNotes: sys.query_store_wait_stats does not exist on SQL Server 2016. Use querystore.wait_stats_summary_2022 on SQL Server 2022+/Azure SQL Database for the secondary-replica identifier.

azureSqlDatabase.notes: Supported; prefer querystore.wait_stats_summary_2022 since Azure SQL Database always runs a current engine.

probes.requiredPermission: VIEW DATABASE STATE (SQL Server 2017-2019) or VIEW DATABASE PERFORMANCE STATE (SQL Server 2022+).

parameters.name: @StartTime
parameters.description: Inclusive lower bound on the runtime-stats interval start_time.

parameters.name: @EndTime
parameters.description: Exclusive upper bound on the runtime-stats interval start_time.

probes.resultContract: Zero or more rows, one per (plan_id, runtime_stats_interval_id, execution_type, wait_category), already SUMmed across duplicate active-interval rows, with total_count_executions joined in from Query Store runtime stats (exec_agg grouped by the matching non-replica keys). All wait-time columns are MILLISECONDS. weighted_avg_query_wait_time_ms_per_execution is CAST to decimal(19,4) before division so bigint/bigint truncation never occurs.

probes.title: Query Store wait statistics with replica identifier (SQL Server 2022+)
probes.versionVariantNotes: replica_group_id does not exist before SQL Server 2022 and raises 'Invalid column name' there. Use querystore.wait_stats_summary_2017 for SQL Server 2017-2019.

azureSqlDatabase.notes: Supported.

probes.requiredPermission: VIEW DATABASE PERFORMANCE STATE on the database.

parameters.name: @StartTime
parameters.description: Inclusive lower bound on the runtime-stats interval start_time.

parameters.name: @EndTime
parameters.description: Exclusive upper bound on the runtime-stats interval start_time.

probes.resultContract: Zero or more rows, one per (plan_id, runtime_stats_interval_id, execution_type, wait_category, replica_group_id), already SUMmed across duplicate active-interval rows, with total_count_executions joined in from an exec_agg CTE grouped by AND joined on replica_group_id (not just plan/interval/execution_type) so one replica's total execution count is never applied to another replica's wait row. All wait-time columns are MILLISECONDS. weighted_avg_query_wait_time_ms_per_execution is CAST to decimal(19,4) before division so bigint/bigint truncation never occurs.

probes.title: Database/file allocated vs. used space

azureSqlDatabase.notes: Supported.

probes.requiredPermission: sys.database_files: ordinary database access. sys.dm_db_file_space_usage: VIEW SERVER STATE (SQL Server 2016-2019) or VIEW SERVER PERFORMANCE STATE (SQL Server 2022+); Azure SQL Database: server admin/Microsoft Entra admin or ##MS_ServerStateReader## membership (Basic/S0/S1/elastic pool), else VIEW DATABASE STATE or ##MS_ServerStateReader## membership.
probes.resultContract: One row per file in the current database. allocated_bytes/data_total_bytes/data_used_bytes are exact bigint byte counts derived from 8-KiB pages. Data fields are NULL for LOG files; log allocated size appears via allocated_bytes, while log usage is reported separately.

probes.title: Transaction log space usage

azureSqlDatabase.notes: Supported.

probes.requiredPermission: VIEW SERVER STATE (SQL Server 2016-2019) or VIEW SERVER PERFORMANCE STATE (SQL Server 2022+). Azure SQL Database: server admin/Microsoft Entra admin or ##MS_ServerStateReader## membership (Basic/S0/S1/elastic pool), else VIEW DATABASE STATE or ##MS_ServerStateReader## membership.
probes.resultContract: Exactly one row for the current database: exact bigint total/used log bytes and used_log_space_in_percent (0-100, relative to total_log_size_in_bytes).

probes.title: Live sessions/requests with current statement text

azureSqlDatabase.notes: Supported, but VIEW DATABASE STATE on Azure SQL Database restricts visibility to the current database's own sessions rather than the whole logical server.

probes.requiredPermission: VIEW SERVER STATE (SQL Server 2019 and earlier; VIEW DATABASE STATE on Azure SQL Database) or VIEW SERVER PERFORMANCE STATE (SQL Server 2022+).

parameters.name: @IncludeIdleSessions
parameters.description: When false, only sessions with an active request are returned.

parameters.name: @MinElapsedMs
parameters.description: Lower bound on total_elapsed_time (ms) for the active request; use to focus on long-running requests.

parameters.name: @DatabaseId
parameters.description: When supplied, restricts active requests to their request database and idle sessions to their current session database. NULL returns all visible user sessions/requests.

probes.resultContract: Zero or more rows, one per (session_id, request_id). Idle rows have NULL request_id and use the session's current database_id/name; active rows use the request database. current_statement_text is the offset-resolved substring of the executing statement; batch_text is the full submitted batch. No plan XML is fetched.

probes.title: Current waiting task queue

azureSqlDatabase.notes: Supported.

probes.requiredPermission: VIEW SERVER STATE (SQL Server 2019 and earlier) or VIEW SERVER PERFORMANCE STATE (SQL Server 2022+).

parameters.name: @MinWaitMs
parameters.description: Lower bound on wait_duration_ms.

probes.resultContract: Zero or more rows, one per waiting task, preserving exec_context_id and the raw blocking_session_id sentinel values (NULL, -2, -3, -4, -5) documented in sql/README.md; the application interprets them, this probe never rewrites them.

probes.title: Root-blocker input facts (no graph construction)

azureSqlDatabase.notes: Supported, subject to the same VIEW DATABASE STATE visibility restriction as sessions.active_requests.

probes.requiredPermission: VIEW SERVER STATE (SQL Server 2019 and earlier) or VIEW SERVER PERFORMANCE STATE (SQL Server 2022+).
probes.resultContract: Zero or more rows tagged by fact_source ('blocked_request' or 'idle_open_transaction'). Returns facts only; the application builds any blocking graph and determines the root blocker itself. Raw blocking_session_id sentinel values are preserved. idle_open_transaction is deduplicated to exactly one row per session_id via MAX(open_transaction_count), because sys.dm_tran_session_transactions can return multiple rows per session under MARS.

probes.title: Query memory grant requests and holders

azureSqlDatabase.notes: Supported; scheduler_id/wait_order/pool_id/group_id are filtered to NULL by the engine to avoid exposing cross-tenant placement information.

probes.requiredPermission: VIEW SERVER STATE (SQL Server 2019 and earlier; VIEW DATABASE STATE on Azure SQL Database) or VIEW SERVER PERFORMANCE STATE (SQL Server 2022+).
probes.resultContract: Zero or more rows, one per (session_id, request_id) with a memory grant request. Memory columns are KiB. grant_time IS NULL means still waiting for a grant (non-NULL once granted); wait_time_ms is the inverse -- populated only while waiting and NULL once granted. plan_handle/sql_handle are opaque; batch_text is resolved but no Showplan XML is fetched.

probes.title: tempdb file/session/task space usage

azureSqlDatabase.notes: Unsupported: a connection cannot target tempdb as its initial catalog on Azure SQL Database. The session/task space-usage DMVs are documented as applicable only to tempdb, so LiveIncidentCollector reports this evidence as unavailable rather than querying them from a user database.

probes.requiredPermission: VIEW SERVER STATE (SQL Server 2016-2019) or VIEW SERVER PERFORMANCE STATE (SQL Server 2022+).

parameters.name: @IncludeSystemSessions
parameters.description: When false, session_id <= 50 (system sessions) are excluded from the session/task result sets.

probes.resultContract: Three result sets in order: (1) tempdb file space usage, requires the connection's current database to be tempdb; (2) per-session tempdb page allocation; (3) per-task tempdb page allocation with exec_context_id preserved. Page counts converted to MiB where noted.

probes.title: Cumulative per-file I/O counters (instance-wide, joins sys.master_files)

azureSqlDatabase.notes: Joins sys.master_files, which is not available on Azure SQL Database (only SQL Server, SQL Managed Instance, and Analytics Platform System). Use io.file_io_stats_current_db on Azure SQL Database instead; it joins sys.database_files and is bounded to the current database.

probes.requiredPermission: VIEW SERVER STATE (SQL Server 2019 and earlier) or VIEW SERVER PERFORMANCE STATE (SQL Server 2022+).
probes.resultContract: One row per (database_id, file_id) visible to the caller. The application computes deltas between polls. *_ms columns are milliseconds; byte columns are raw bytes, not pages. sample_ms is milliseconds since the COMPUTER (OS) started, not since the last Database Engine restart; the underlying counters reset when the SQL Server service restarts, a different and typically more frequent event than an OS reboot, so sample_ms regression alone cannot be used to detect a counter reset. Detect a reset via sys.dm_os_sys_info.sqlserver_start_time changing between polls, or via any counter reading lower than the previous poll for the same file.

probes.title: Cumulative per-file I/O counters (current database, Azure-safe)
probes.versionVariantNotes: Bounded to the current database (DB_ID()) and joins sys.database_files instead of sys.master_files, so it runs on Azure SQL Database where io.file_io_stats does not.

azureSqlDatabase.notes: Supported; sys.dm_io_virtual_file_stats(DB_ID(), NULL) and sys.database_files are both current-database-scoped and available on Azure SQL Database.

probes.requiredPermission: VIEW SERVER STATE (SQL Server 2019 and earlier) or VIEW SERVER PERFORMANCE STATE (SQL Server 2022+). Azure SQL Database: server admin/Microsoft Entra admin or ##MS_ServerStateReader## membership (Basic/S0/S1/elastic pool), else VIEW DATABASE STATE or ##MS_ServerStateReader## membership.
probes.resultContract: One row per file_id in the current database. The application computes deltas between polls. *_ms columns are milliseconds; byte columns are raw bytes, not pages. sample_ms is milliseconds since the COMPUTER (OS) started, not since the last Database Engine restart; detect an engine restart via sys.dm_os_sys_info.sqlserver_start_time changing between polls, or via counter regression, not via sample_ms alone.

probes.title: Scheduler CPU/runnable-queue pressure (base, SQL Server 2016-2018)
probes.versionVariantNotes: Base column set only; omits ideal_workers_limit, a SQL Server 2019 (15.x)-only column that raises Invalid column name on 2016 (13.x)/2017 (14.x). Use scheduler.pressure_2019 on SQL Server 2019+/Azure SQL Database for that column.

azureSqlDatabase.notes: Supported, subject to the tiered permission rules in sql/README.md, but prefer scheduler.pressure_2019 on Azure SQL Database since it always runs a current engine. The visible scheduler count reflects the database's assigned vCore/DTU allocation, not a physical host's processor count.

probes.requiredPermission: VIEW SERVER STATE (SQL Server 2019 and earlier) or VIEW SERVER PERFORMANCE STATE (SQL Server 2022+). Azure SQL Database: server admin/Microsoft Entra admin or ##MS_ServerStateReader## membership (Basic/S0/S1/elastic pool), else VIEW DATABASE STATE or ##MS_ServerStateReader## membership.
probes.resultContract: One row per VISIBLE ONLINE scheduler (hidden/internal schedulers excluded). Cumulative CPU/delay columns since engine start; runnable_tasks_count > 0 with a high current_tasks_count signals CPU pressure.

probes.title: Scheduler CPU/runnable-queue pressure (adds ideal_workers_limit, SQL Server 2019+)
probes.versionVariantNotes: Adds ideal_workers_limit (SQL Server 2019 (15.x)+ only); selecting it on 2016 (13.x)/2017 (14.x) raises Invalid column name, not NULL. Use scheduler.pressure_2016 on older engines.

azureSqlDatabase.notes: Supported, subject to the tiered permission rules in sql/README.md. The visible scheduler count reflects the database's assigned vCore/DTU allocation, not a physical host's processor count.

probes.requiredPermission: VIEW SERVER STATE (SQL Server 2019 and earlier) or VIEW SERVER PERFORMANCE STATE (SQL Server 2022+). Azure SQL Database: server admin/Microsoft Entra admin or ##MS_ServerStateReader## membership (Basic/S0/S1/elastic pool), else VIEW DATABASE STATE or ##MS_ServerStateReader## membership.
probes.resultContract: One row per VISIBLE ONLINE scheduler (hidden/internal schedulers excluded). Cumulative CPU/delay columns since engine start; runnable_tasks_count > 0 with a high current_tasks_count signals CPU pressure; ideal_workers_limit gives the engine's estimated worker-thread concurrency ceiling for that scheduler.

probes.title: Index seek/scan/lookup/update counts

azureSqlDatabase.notes: Supported; rows for other databases are silently filtered by the engine.

probes.requiredPermission: SQL Server/Managed Instance: VIEW SERVER STATE (SQL Server 2016-2019) or VIEW SERVER PERFORMANCE STATE (SQL Server 2022+). Azure SQL Database: server admin/Microsoft Entra admin or ##MS_ServerStateReader## membership (Basic/S0/S1/elastic pool), else VIEW DATABASE STATE or ##MS_ServerStateReader## membership.
probes.resultContract: Zero or more rows, one per (object_id, index_id) touched since counters last reset. An index with no row here has not been used, not that it is empty. Counters reset only on Database Engine restart, or on database detach/shutdown (e.g. AUTO_CLOSE), which removes rows for that database entirely; no official documentation attributes a reset to index rebuild. Excludes memory-optimized and spatial indexes.

probes.title: Targeted index operational (lock/latch) statistics

azureSqlDatabase.notes: Supported.

probes.requiredPermission: CONTROL permission on the specified object (this probe's normal, single-object use). Passing NULL for @ObjectId to request all objects in the database (not a supported use of this probe) would additionally require VIEW DATABASE STATE (SQL Server 2016-2019) or VIEW DATABASE PERFORMANCE STATE (SQL Server 2022+); a NULL @DatabaseId for all databases would additionally require VIEW SERVER STATE/VIEW SERVER PERFORMANCE STATE. VIEW DATABASE (PERFORMANCE) STATE grants/denies override a per-object CONTROL grant/deny.

parameters.name: @ObjectId
parameters.description: object_id of the table/view to inspect. Must not be supplied as NULL: NULL here (with NULL index/partition) forces a resource-intensive whole-database enumeration, because sys.dm_db_index_operational_stats treats NULL/0/DEFAULT for this parameter identically as a wildcard. The query wraps the parameter in COALESCE(@ObjectId, -1) as a fail-safe so a NULL argument returns zero rows instead of triggering that enumeration. Resolve a specific object first via index.usage_summary or OBJECT_ID().

parameters.name: @IndexId
parameters.description: NULL returns all indexes on @ObjectId.

parameters.name: @PartitionNumber
parameters.description: NULL returns all partitions.

probes.resultContract: Zero or more rows, one per (object_id, index_id, partition_number). Wait columns are milliseconds; count columns are raw counts. Counters exist only as long as the metadata-cache entry for the heap/B-tree does; they reset to zero on metadata (re)caching (e.g. restart or failover) and disappear when the object/index/partition is dropped or truncated, and certain other DDL can reset them to zero without a drop -- this is not simply 'since last restart or rebuild'.

probes.title: Server-scoped effective permission check

azureSqlDatabase.notes: Supported, but Azure SQL Database enforces database-scoped VIEW DATABASE STATE in place of most server-scoped permissions; the negotiator must additionally run capability.database_permission_check there rather than relying on this probe alone.

probes.requiredPermission: HAS_PERMS_BY_NAME(): none (public). It reports only the caller's own effective permission and never another principal's.

parameters.name: @Permission
parameters.description: Server-scoped permission name to evaluate, e.g. 'VIEW SERVER STATE' or 'VIEW SERVER PERFORMANCE STATE'.

probes.resultContract: Exactly one row: has_permission is 1/0/NULL (NULL when the securable/permission combination cannot be evaluated on this platform).

probes.title: Database-scoped effective permission check

azureSqlDatabase.notes: Supported; this is the database-scoped counterpart required on Azure SQL Database, where most session/wait DMVs require VIEW DATABASE STATE rather than VIEW SERVER STATE.

probes.requiredPermission: HAS_PERMS_BY_NAME(): none (public). It reports only the caller's own effective permission and never another principal's.

parameters.name: @Permission
parameters.description: Database-scoped permission name to evaluate, e.g. 'VIEW DATABASE STATE' or 'VIEW DATABASE PERFORMANCE STATE'.

probes.resultContract: Exactly one row: has_permission is 1/0/NULL (NULL when the securable/permission combination cannot be evaluated on this platform), always evaluated against the connection's own current database.

probes.title: Query Store plan/runtime-stats catalog metadata for PSP/OPPO/secondary-replica detection

azureSqlDatabase.notes: Supported; Azure SQL Database always runs a current engine, so both plan_type_desc and replica_group_id are present there.

probes.requiredPermission: sys.all_columns / OBJECT_ID(): none (public). Reads catalog metadata only; no Query Store data rows are read.
probes.resultContract: Zero to four rows, one per (view_name, column_name) pair present on this engine build. Row absence for a given column is the reliable signal that the column, and the feature it backs, does not exist here; major version alone is never trusted for this.

probes.title: Azure SQL Database tenant CPU/memory compute limits

azureSqlDatabase.notes: Supported; this probe exists specifically for Azure SQL Database and must not be run against SQL Server on-premises or Azure SQL Managed Instance, where sys.dm_user_db_resource_governance does not apply.

probes.requiredPermission: sys.dm_user_db_resource_governance: VIEW DATABASE STATE (or VIEW DATABASE PERFORMANCE STATE) on Azure SQL Database. sys.dm_os_job_object: none additional beyond database connectivity there.
probes.resultContract: Zero or one row: cpu_limit (NULL for DTU-based databases) and process_memory_limit_mb for the current tenant database.
